newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares tumble, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares tumble, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares on Friday fell sharply for the second day running and analysts said another fall possible on Monday, in part because of nervousness over a possible interest-rate rise in the United States in late March.

"It seems yesterday's and today's falls were stimulated by the situation on world markets...mainly on the American market. I don't know if that's rational but that's what's happening," said Pawel Tarnowski of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.

Tarnowski said Friday's information of a deeper than expected slide in U.S. wholesale prices, which cheered some Western bourses in the view that U.S. rates would remain stable, could lead to growth in Warsaw on Monday.
But he said subsequent falls were still possible.
Analysts said investors were also taking profits after recent gains, especially domestic investors benefiting from recent rises by small-cap stocks.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 4.2 percent to 16,687.1 points and turnover rose 50.2 percent to 232 million zlotys ($75.1 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 86 to one with two stocks flat.

Twelve main-market stocks fell more than nine percent on Friday, with engineering firm Prochem, last week's market leader, falling 10 percent with post-price-fixing selling strong enough for players to have their bids reduced.

Trade in builder Espebepe was suspended as its creditors meet to discuss a possible debt write off. Mass privatisation NFI units fell 2.8 percent in regular trade and 0.3 percent in continuous trade, where stocks were mixed.
